Base directory for this skill: /data3/paper_analysis/.claude/skills/paper-experiment-idea

# Paper Experiment Idea

## Parameters

调用本 skill 时，用户**必须**提供以下三个路径参数：

| 参数 | 说明 | 示例 |
|------|------|------|
| `{{paper_dir}}` | 论文 PDF 所在目录 | `papers/paper_2026/` |
| `{{experiment_dir}}` | 实验分层 Markdown 文件输出目录 | `experiment_repo/` |
| `{{idea_dir}}` | 设计思路 Markdown 文件输出目录 | `idea_repo/` |

## Overview

根据所给论文标题，在 `{{paper_dir}}` 目录中找到原文PDF。阅读全文，提取复现论文实验所需的软硬件信息，按照实现和实验分层次输出到 `{{experiment_dir}}`，并提取设计思路输出到 `{{idea_dir}}`。

## Workflow

### 第一步：定位论文PDF

1. 根据用户提供的论文标题、编号、文件名或标识符，在 `{{paper_dir}}` 目录中搜索原始PDF。
2. 搜索策略：使用 `rg --files`、标题片段、论文编号和可能的文件名变体进行匹配。
3. 如果用户只给出编号，先通过 `paper_titles.md` 等本地标题列表进行映射。
4. 优先使用可读全文，顺序为：配套提取的 `.txt`/`.md` > PDF文本提取 > 官方论文HTML > 其他本地笔记。不要仅依赖摘要或二手总结。

### 第二步：阅读论文实现与实验章节

阅读以下最有助于实验提取的章节：

- Implementation / Experiment / Evaluation / Experimental Setup
- Method / Design / Architecture / Approach
- Introduction / Motivation / Background

基于以上章节总结：

- 论文如何实现 baseline
- 论文如何实现所提出的创新设计
- 使用了哪些硬件平台、模拟器、框架、模型、数据集或 benchmark
- 为了复现，从联网搜索或从原文查找是否开源和开原链接

### 第三步：实验分层与输出

按实现和实验对论文的实验和实现分层次，输出到 `{{experiment_dir}}` 目录下的对应层次 md 文件。论文实现可以包含多个层次，对应多个层次 md 文件中写入要求内容。不完全匹配的按照最相似/最接近来分层并反馈。

### 第四步：设计思路提取

基于论文实现归属的层次，和论文原文中的 Introduction、Motivation、Background 和 Method 章节，说明论文通过什么具体设计解决 Baseline 的痛点，输出到 `{{idea_dir}}/idea库.md`。

## 证据规则

- 信息以论文原文为准。若细节缺失，写 `论文未明确说明` 而非自行编造。
- 保留模型、数据集、框架、模拟器、benchmark、芯片、GPU、RTL工具、kernel、指标等具体名称。
- 若论文给出模拟器或工具名称但未给链接，先在论文中搜索URL；必要时用联网搜索，无法确认则写明无法确认。
- 将"baseline 实现"理解为论文实际评估的具体版本，而非仅是一般性的先前工作概念。
- 保持文字简洁、技术化、便于后续复现使用。

## 实验层次分类

将每篇论文的实现和实验按以下层次分类。一篇论文可属于多个层次，每个匹配的层次对应一个追加条目。

### 算法pipeline

适用条件：实现是通过稀疏、压缩、量化、蒸馏、共享或近似权重/激活等方式加速算法推理，同时保证准确率，或者提出新的算法模型。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_算法pipeline.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于算法pipeline的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 硬件平台是什么，配置是什么。
- 模型是什么。数据集和bench分别是什么。
- 开源情况。基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释，解释算法pipeline。
```

### Serving调度

适用条件：实现是修改开源Serving框架来优化多请求调度，满足SLO要求或提高吞吐量等。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_Serving调度.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于Serving调度的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 硬件平台是什么，配置是什么。
- 开源Serving框架是什么。修改了什么。
- 开源情况。Serving框架如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
```

### 编译框架

适用条件：实现是修改编译框架实现，进行自动化kernel生成，保证性能等要求。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_编译框架.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于编译框架的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 硬件平台是什么，配置是什么。
- 开源编译框架是什么。修改了什么。
- 开源情况。编译框架如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
```

### kernel调度

适用条件：实现是新的kernel算子或稀疏/量化/传输等运行时计算和kernel算子在不同后端平台（GPU、异构、PIM、加速器等）的调度。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_kernel调度.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于kernel调度/运行时计算的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 后端平台是什么，配置是什么。
- 评估性能的软件/脚本是什么。修改了什么。
- 开源情况。评估软件/脚本如何使用？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
```

### 硬件架构

适用条件：实现是RTL实现IP模块或仿真器修改，来让硬件支持完成运行时计算、Tile指令、pipeline、访存、存内计算等，在workload下提升性能，并评估面积、功耗等。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_硬件架构.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于硬件架构的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
```

### 芯片设计

适用条件：实现是和物理架构关联的优化，如chiplet、Wafer-Scale Engine、DRAM、RERAM等芯片结构优化。

追加到 `{{experiment_dir}}/实验_芯片设计.md`：

```md
## <论文标题>

- 属于芯片设计的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
```

## 设计思路条目

在实验分层完成后，追加一条设计思路到 `{{idea_dir}}/idea库.md`。使用论文的 Introduction、Motivation、Background 和 Method/Design 章节，说明论文通过什么具体设计解决 Baseline 的痛点。

```md
## <论文标题>

- baseline方法是什么？
  <说明baseline方法，并给出baseline在模型推理算法-系统框架-编译框架-kernel调度-硬件架构全栈的执行例子。缺失层次写"论文未明确说明"。>

- 论文方法是什么？如何对应解决Baseline的缺陷？
  <说明论文方法，并对比baseline给出论文方法在模型推理算法-系统框架-编译框架-kernel调度-硬件架构全栈的执行例子。缺失层次写"论文未明确说明"。>
```

全栈执行例子应具体而非穷举。好的回答沿着一个请求、token、tensor、tile、kernel、内存传输或芯片级数据路径，穿过论文支持的尽可能多的层次。

## 质量检查

完成前确认：

- 验证每个追加的文件路径存在且包含新条目。
- 验证目标论文尽可能通过 `{{paper_dir}}` 解析，若非 `{{paper_dir}}` 来源则说明。
- 确保同一论文在同一目标文件中不重复（除非用户明确要求再次处理）。
- 确认每个实验层次条目包含比较目标/baseline、提出的实现、评估的硬件/模拟器/框架。
- 确认设计思路条目直接将 baseline 缺陷映射到方法设计选择。
- 在最终回复中列出更新的文件、任何缺失证据、以及近似层次匹配情况。

418	Current PIM systems employ a PIM-specific BIOS update
419	to maintain separate physical address spaces for PIM and
420	DRAM [77], [106]. This design decision is due to the limitations coming from existing DRAM-specific protocols (e.g.,
421	DDR4 [98]), which dictate a deterministic latency behavior. To
422	better explain the intricacy of our problem in hand, consider
423	the example in Figure 2(a) where both the host processor and
424	the PIM core tries to access the same memory bank within
425	the PIM device simultaneously. Such situation complicates the
426	task for the baseline host-side memory controller in managing
427	this structural hazard, unless it is heavily modified to properly
428	handle this conflicting scenarios. For instance, the memory
429	controller would have to arbitrate memory accesses between
430	the host processor and PIM core, which can lead to violation of
431	the DRAM-specific protocols as their access latency changes
432	(i.e., arbitration cannot guarantee deterministic latency). Consequently, PIM manufacturers have designed their systems
433	to prevent this situation from happening by employing the
434	following two techniques. First, only a single entity, either the
435	host processor (Figure 2(b)) or the PIM core (Figure 2(c)), can
436	access the PIM address space at any given time. This design
437	decision obviates the need to modify the host processor’s
438	memory controller, easing PIM’s integration in conventional
439	systems. Second, fine-grained address interleaving employed
440	in conventional memory mapping (Figure 1(d)) is disabled so
441	that it prevents segments of both the DRAM and PIM physical
442	addresses from being mapped to the same memory bank.
443	As depicted in Figure 2(d), having parts of the DRAM and
444	PIM physical address both be mapped at a common memory
445	bank causes the resource conflicting scenario discussed in
446	Figure 2(a). As such, the PIM-specific memory mapping in
447	current PIM systems make sure that the physical DRAM (and
448	PIM) addresses are mapped locally within a DRAM (and PIM)
449	DIMM (Figure 2(e)). A tradeoff made with this design is
450	that the PIM programmer must explicitly copy data across the
451	DRAM address space and the PIM address space, whenever a
452	data is offloaded from DRAM to PIM, and vice versa.

753	C. UPMEM-PIM Hardware/Software Architecture
754	Hardware architecture. UPMEM-PIM is based on
755	a DDR4-2400 DIMM form factor, equipped with eight
756	UPMEM-PIM chips per rank. Each UPMEM-PIM chip contains eight PIM cores (called DPUs by UPMEM), one PIM
757	core per each DRAM bank. A single host CPU can support
758	up to 1,280 PIM cores and a single PIM core is capable of
759	achieving a peak memory bandwidth of 1 GB/s, allowing the
760	aggregate memory bandwidth to exceed 1 TB/sec.
761	Programming model. Similar to CUDA [89], UPMEMPIM adopts the co-processor computing model, where the
762	CPU offloads a memory-intensive task to PIM. To offload a
763	task to UPMEM-PIM, programmers are required to write two
764	distinct segments of code: the PIM-side code and the hostside code. In the PIM-side code, the programmer describes
765	the task to be offloaded to PIM which follows the singleprogram multiple-data (SPMD) model, i.e., a single program
766	gets executed by multiple PIM cores. Within the host-side
767	code, the programmer designates the total number of PIM
768	cores to utilize, which input data to transfer over to the
769	PIM address space (DRAM→PIM), and which output results
770	derived by the PIM cores to transfer back into the DRAM
771	address space (PIM→DRAM), all of which is programmed
772	using APIs provided in UPMEM-PIM’s software stack.
773	Runtime library for data transfers. The UPMEM-PIM
774	runtime library offers a layer of abstraction that hides low-level
775	details of the PIM hardware from the programmer, one notable
776	example being the need for preprocessing data before they
777	are transferred over to PIM. The need for data preprocessing
778	arises due to the way chip interleaving is employed within the
779	DIMM. Each data word (8 bytes) is partitioned in a 1-byte
780	granularity and distributed across multiple UPMEM-PIM chips
781	(8 UPMEM-PIM chips in a ×8 configuration), an example
782	we illustrate in Figure 3(a). Such data interleaving across
783	UPMEM-PIM chips presents a significant challenge for PIM
784	computation because each (bank-level) PIM core only receives
785	a fraction of a data word. To address this issue, the UPMEMPIM runtime library transposes the data into an (8×8) byte
786	matrix and copies the transposed matrix across the 8 UPMEMPIM chips, allowing each PIM core to receive the full 8-byte

Abstract—Processing-in-memory (PIM) has emerged as a
promising solution for accelerating memory-intensive workloads
as they provide high memory bandwidth to the processing units.
This approach has drawn attention not only from the academic
community but also from the industry, leading to the development
of real-world commercial PIM devices. In this work, we first
conduct an in-depth characterization on UPMEM’s generalpurpose PIM system and analyze the bottlenecks caused by the
data transfers across the DRAM and PIM address space. Our
characterization study reveals several critical challenges associated with DRAM↔PIM data transfers in memory bus integrated
PIM systems, for instance, its high CPU core utilization, high
power consumption, and low read/write throughput for both
DRAM and PIM. Driven by our key findings, we introduce
the PIM-MMU architecture which is a hardware/software codesign that enables energy-efficient DRAM↔PIM transfers for
PIM systems. PIM-MMU synergistically combines a hardwarebased data copy engine, a PIM-optimized memory scheduler,
and a heterogeneity-aware memory mapping function, the utilization of which is supported by our PIM-MMU software
stack, significantly improving the efficiency of DRAM↔PIM data
transfers. Experimental results show that PIM-MMU improves
the DRAM↔PIM data transfer throughput by an average 4.1×
and enhances its energy-efficiency by 4.1×, leading to a 2.2×
end-to-end speedup for real-world PIM workloads.
Index Terms—Processing-in-memory; near-memory processing; parallel architecture

I. I NTRODUCTION
Modern data-intensive workloads (e.g., AI inference tasks
for large language models [10], [17], [40], [47], [48], [92],
[97], [114], recommendation systems [63], [72], [73], [86], and
graph processing [2], [19], [35], [113], [117]) are memorybound as they pose unprecedented demand for large data.
Despite the increasing demand for high memory bandwidth,
integrating a larger number of DRAM I/O pins at the processor
die is challenging because of form factor constraints and issues
related to signal integrity [67].
To address such limitation, processing-in-memory (PIM)
architectures gained interest by integrating compute logic close
to DRAM. Because of its potential to alleviate the memory
bandwidth bottleneck modern processors face, PIM has been
extensively explored in both academia [2], [3], [8], [9], [15],
[23], [24], [28], [29], [34], [45], [49], [50], [66], [78], [90],

To this end, we propose a Memory Management Unit
for PIM (PIM-MMU) which is designed to fundamentally
address the challenges associated with DRAM↔PIM data
transfers in memory bus integrated PIM system, synergistically
combining the following three key components:
Data Copy Engine. In our proposed system, PIM programmers are provided with a software interface that
completely offloads DRAM↔PIM data transfers to a
Data Copy Engine (DCE). DCE not only handles the
data copy operations but also the data preprocessing operations (e.g., data transpose), accelerating the end-to-end
DRAM↔PIM data transfers without CPU intervention.
• PIM-aware Memory Scheduler. To overcome the limitations of PIM’s software-based coarse-grained memory
scheduling, we propose a hardware-based, PIM-aware
Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS) which is integrated inside
our DCE. PIM-MS enhances PIM read/write throughput
by leveraging the unique properties of DRAM↔PIM
data transfers where coarse-grained data copy operations targeting different PIM cores (designated by PIM
programmers at the software level) can be reordered
without affecting program correctness. PIM-MS utilizes
such property to enable fine-grained memory scheduling
at the hardware level, drastically improving MLP and thus
the PIM read/write throughput.
• Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit. We also introduce a unique hardware-based memory mapping architecture named Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit
(HetMap) that enables PIM-MMU to separate the address
space of DRAM and PIM while also enabling high
DRAM read/write throughput. HetMap maintains a dual
set of memory mapping functions: (1) an MLP-centric
mapping function for memory transactions targeting the
normal DRAM address space, and (2) a locality-centric
mapping function that is designed to honor the per-bank
PIM address spaces by localizing the mapped regions
within each PIM core’s memory bank.

that translates a physical address to a DRAM address
partitions the data and distributes them across the DRAM
subsystem in fine granularity to maximize memory-level

parallelism. Such fine-grained “hardware-based” memory mapping architecture (and the associated memory

requests evenly across the memory channels [82]. However,
the frequency in which bits within the address closer to the
LSB change can vary depending on the program’s memory
access pattern. To better accommodate such variability, advanced memory mapping functions utilize XOR hashing [115].
Specifically, XOR hashing takes multiple physical address bits,
from the LSB to the most significant bit (MSB), to compute
the channel address which enables the DRAM subsystem to
better adapt to diverse memory access patterns.
In modern high-end server class x86 CPUs (or GPUs), the
memory mapping function can be customized by adjusting the
BIOS configuration (or vBIOS in the context of GPUs [99]).
In Intel Xeon CPUs, for instance, the BIOS configuration
provides a knob to enable (aka N-way) or disable (aka 1-way)
address interleaving across different hierarchical levels of the
DRAM subsystem (Figure 1). Turning on N-way interleaving
that targets a specific DRAM subsystem (e.g., Integrated
Memory Controller (IMC) level interleaving, channel level
interleaving, . . .) thus enables the memory mapping function
to exploit MLP at that particular DRAM subsystem. As shown
in Figure 1(b), configuring the memory mapping function
as 1-way interleaving for both IMC level and channel level
positions their corresponding address bits closer to the MSB,
making it challenging to fully exploit MLP. Conversely, in the
configuration shown in Figure 1(c), adjusting channel level
interleaving to N-way moves the channel bits closer to the
LSB, which helps better exploit MLP. However, maintaining
the IMC level interleaving at 1-way results in the IMC bits to
be placed near the MSB, rendering the lower physical address
space to be mapped only at channels 0 and 1, connected to
IMC0 (and the higher physical address space to be mapped at
channel 2 and 3, connected to IMC1). To fully exploit MLP,
the BIOS must be configured as N-way interleaving across all
DRAM subsystems which positions both the IMC and channel
bits closer to the LSB (Figure 1(d)).

conventional DRAM. Below we discuss the unique address
space management employed in memory bus integrated PIM.
Current PIM systems employ a PIM-specific BIOS update
to maintain separate physical address spaces for PIM and
DRAM [77], [106]. This design decision is due to the limitations coming from existing DRAM-specific protocols (e.g.,
DDR4 [98]), which dictate a deterministic latency behavior. To
better explain the intricacy of our problem in hand, consider
the example in Figure 2(a) where both the host processor and
the PIM core tries to access the same memory bank within
the PIM device simultaneously. Such situation complicates the
task for the baseline host-side memory controller in managing
this structural hazard, unless it is heavily modified to properly
handle this conflicting scenarios. For instance, the memory
controller would have to arbitrate memory accesses between
the host processor and PIM core, which can lead to violation of
the DRAM-specific protocols as their access latency changes
(i.e., arbitration cannot guarantee deterministic latency). Consequently, PIM manufacturers have designed their systems
to prevent this situation from happening by employing the
following two techniques. First, only a single entity, either the
host processor (Figure 2(b)) or the PIM core (Figure 2(c)), can
access the PIM address space at any given time. This design
decision obviates the need to modify the host processor’s
memory controller, easing PIM’s integration in conventional
systems. Second, fine-grained address interleaving employed
in conventional memory mapping (Figure 1(d)) is disabled so
that it prevents segments of both the DRAM and PIM physical
addresses from being mapped to the same memory bank.
As depicted in Figure 2(d), having parts of the DRAM and
PIM physical address both be mapped at a common memory
bank causes the resource conflicting scenario discussed in
Figure 2(a). As such, the PIM-specific memory mapping in
current PIM systems make sure that the physical DRAM (and
PIM) addresses are mapped locally within a DRAM (and PIM)
DIMM (Figure 2(e)). A tradeoff made with this design is
that the PIM programmer must explicitly copy data across the
DRAM address space and the PIM address space, whenever a
data is offloaded from DRAM to PIM, and vice versa.

When it comes to the actual DRAM↔PIM data transfer
implementation (using dpu_push_xfer [106]), the runtime
library employs several software optimizations to enhance the
DRAM↔PIM data transfer throughput. These include (1) the

C. UPMEM-PIM Hardware/Software Architecture
Hardware architecture. UPMEM-PIM is based on
a DDR4-2400 DIMM form factor, equipped with eight
UPMEM-PIM chips per rank. Each UPMEM-PIM chip contains eight PIM cores (called DPUs by UPMEM), one PIM
core per each DRAM bank. A single host CPU can support
up to 1,280 PIM cores and a single PIM core is capable of
achieving a peak memory bandwidth of 1 GB/s, allowing the
aggregate memory bandwidth to exceed 1 TB/sec.
Programming model. Similar to CUDA [89], UPMEMPIM adopts the co-processor computing model, where the
CPU offloads a memory-intensive task to PIM. To offload a
task to UPMEM-PIM, programmers are required to write two
distinct segments of code: the PIM-side code and the hostside code. In the PIM-side code, the programmer describes
the task to be offloaded to PIM which follows the singleprogram multiple-data (SPMD) model, i.e., a single program
gets executed by multiple PIM cores. Within the host-side
code, the programmer designates the total number of PIM
cores to utilize, which input data to transfer over to the
PIM address space (DRAM→PIM), and which output results
derived by the PIM cores to transfer back into the DRAM
address space (PIM→DRAM), all of which is programmed
using APIs provided in UPMEM-PIM’s software stack.
Runtime library for data transfers. The UPMEM-PIM
runtime library offers a layer of abstraction that hides low-level
details of the PIM hardware from the programmer, one notable
example being the need for preprocessing data before they
are transferred over to PIM. The need for data preprocessing
arises due to the way chip interleaving is employed within the
DIMM. Each data word (8 bytes) is partitioned in a 1-byte
granularity and distributed across multiple UPMEM-PIM chips
(8 UPMEM-PIM chips in a ×8 configuration), an example
we illustrate in Figure 3(a). Such data interleaving across
UPMEM-PIM chips presents a significant challenge for PIM
computation because each (bank-level) PIM core only receives
a fraction of a data word. To address this issue, the UPMEMPIM runtime library transposes the data into an (8×8) byte
matrix and copies the transposed matrix across the 8 UPMEMPIM chips, allowing each PIM core to receive the full 8-byte

physical addresses for DRAM and PIM, necessitating explicit
DRAM↔PIM data transfers (Section II-B). As we quantify in
Section VI, the latency to transfer data across these two regions
incur significant performance overhead, accounting to as much
as 99.7% (average 63.7%) of end-to-end execution time of our
evaluated PIM workloads [43]. Such observation is inline with

root-cause the reason behind the sub-optimal performance of
DRAM↔PIM data transfers.
B. System Characterization and Key Challenges
(Challenge #1) High CPU core utilization and power
consumption. The DRAM→PIM data transfer involves three
main stages: (1) reading from DRAM, (2) preprocessing, (3)

Examples assume that channels 0, 1, 2 are (read) source channels
and channels 3, 4, 5 are (write) destination channels. We measure
the per-channel write throughput using Intel VTune [56] by executing
microbenchmarks over real UPMEM-PIM systems. Section V details

PIM→DRAM transfers. Our first key observation is that, because the CPU is in charge of orchestrating the entire process
of data transfers, it significantly taxes the host processor,
leading to high power overheads. Figure 4 illustrates the effect
of DRAM↔PIM data transfers on CPU core utilization and
system power consumption. As discussed in Section II-C, the
data transfer operation in the UPMEM-PIM runtime library
is implemented using AVX-512 vector load/store instructions,
which are known to be power hungry [39], [105]. Consequently, data transfers across DRAM vs. PIM addresses push
CPU core utilization to near maximum levels and reach close
to 70 Watts of system power consumption.
Despite such high power overheads, DRAM↔PIM data
transfers exhibit limited efficiency from a throughput perspective, significantly underutilizing available memory bandwidth.
Below we root-cause the reason behind why contemporary
PIM system achieves such low data transfer throughput.
(Challenge #2) Sub-optimal PIM read/write throughput.
Conventional DRAM systems are provisioned with MLPenhancing microarchitectural support. For instance, the memory mapping function, which translates physical addresses to
DRAM addresses, partitions/distributes the data across the
DRAM subsystem in fine granularity to maximize MLP. Such
“hardware-based” memory mapping is entirely transparent to
the software layer and helps evenly distribute the memory
read/write traffic across the memory channels (Figure 5(a)).
In contrast, UPMEM-PIM is unable to fully reap out the
MLP enhancing opportunities inherent within such hardwarebased memory mapping architectures due to its bank-level PIM
design. One key characteristic of bank-level PIM systems is
their need for input data to be made locally available within the
target PIM core’s memory bank (Figure 3(b)), before the PIM
kernel is executed. Consequently, PIM programmers must explicitly designate which input data should be transferred over
to which PIM core’s memory bank using software APIs that
enable DRAM↔PIM data transfers (e.g., dpu_push_xfer
in UPMEM-PIM). Unfortunately, because the transferred data
is targeted for a specific memory bank, it becomes challenging
to fully leverage channel/bank-group/bank-level parallelism
in transferring such data, leading to underutilization of PIM

read/write throughput (Figure 5(b)).
Given the limitation of bank-level PIM architectures in
leveraging MLP, UPMEM-PIM exploits thread-level parallelism (TLP) to maximally utilize available memory bandwidth. As depicted in Figure 5(c), the UPMEM-PIM runtime
library launches multiple software threads for DRAM↔PIM
data transfers by having each thread to perform read/write
operations targeting different levels in the PIM hierarchy
(e.g., thread ID=0 targets PIM channel 0/bank 0 while thread
ID=1 targets PIM channel 1/bank 0, . . .), the goal of which
is to maximize data transfer throughput and MLP. While
utilizing TLP does help improve PIM read/write throughput,
our key observation is that such software-based multi-threaded
approach falls short in fully leveraging MLP for enhanced
performance. This is because the effectiveness of the multithreaded PIM data transfers is contingent upon how the
Operating System (OS) schedules these threads, which may
not necessarily be aligned with the optimal distribution of
data accesses across the PIM hierarchy. In general, the OS
thread scheduling policy prioritize fairness [94] which may not
necessarily lead to threads being scheduled in a manner that
balances its memory accesses across the memory subsystem.
This is natural as the OS is (and should be) unaware of the
existence of PIM. For instance, if the OS thread scheduler
prioritizes the execution of three PIM threads transferring data
in channel A and one thread in channel B during a time
interval of T, channel A will experience a higher concentration of data accesses. To maintain system-wide fairness, the
scheduler may adjust the scheduling priority during the next
time interval of T to allow more threads to execute in channel
B. While such scheduling policy better guarantees fairness,
it can lead to inefficient utilization of memory bandwidth
because certain memory channels are preferentially accessed
for longer periods of time, i.e., time interval T is in the order
of several ms. In Figure 6(a), we illustrate the implication
of such coarse-grained, software-based DRAM→PIM data
transfer. As shown, such software-based approach is not able
to fully utilize MLP due to traffic congestion happening

C. Data Copy Engine (DCE)
The DCE contains the following components: (1) an Address Generation Unit (AGU), (2) PIM-MS, (3) two SRAMbased buffers (data buffer and address buffer), and (4) a
preprocessing unit (Figure 9). We use the example in Figure 11 to illustrate PIM-MMU’s overall dataflow during a
DRAM→PIM data transfer (PIM→DRAM data transfer is
orchestrated similarly but we omit its explanation for brevity).
When the CPU launches the pim_mmu_transfer kernel
for execution, the address buffer is copied with both (1) the
physical DRAM addresses (src_arr) that point to all the
source data arrays (input data array in Figure 11) and
(2) the physical PIM addresses that point to all the destination
locations within PIM (dest_pim_id_arr) to which the
source data will be written into. Each entry in the address
buffer stores the following information: (1) the base DRAM
address of the source input data array (DRAM addr field in
Figure 11), (2) the destination PIM core’s ID (PIM addr
field), and (3) an offset counter value (Offset field) that
keeps track of the total number of data elements successfully read from the source data. A data transfer operation
is managed by the PIM-MS, which not only decides which
memory requests to schedule to the DRAM subsystem (PIMMS’s memory scheduling algorithm and the key intuitions that
drive its design is detailed in the following Section IV-D), but
it also goes over the address buffer entries and coordinates
the translation of the source/destination physical addresses
to DRAM/PIM addresses with the memory controller. In the
example in Figure 11, we will assume that PIM-MS has chosen
to transfer data targeting PIM core ID=511. PIM-MS first reads
an entry from the address buffer (step ❶ in Figure 11) and
sends it to the AGU (step ❷). The AGU then translates the
source physical address to the corresponding DRAM address
with the memory controller and places the translated memory
read request to the memory controller’s read request queue.
These two steps (❶,❷) are iteratively done over all the entries
in the address buffer until the memory controller’s request
queue is full. When the memory controller services a read
operation (step ❸), the retrieved data is temporarily stored

1673	D. PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS)
1674	We now discuss the design principles behind our PIMMS. The key observation that drives PIM-MS’s design is
1675	that memory transactions targeting the PIM address space
1676	(for both reads and writes) during DRAM↔PIM data transfer
1677	are guaranteed to have mutually exclusive addresses. Such
1678	mutual exclusiveness ensures that there are no true data
1679	dependencies across different PIM memory transactions. To
1680	better understand this unique property, it is important to
1681	understand how PIM programmers go about partitioning input/output data. Before computation begins on the PIM cores,
1682	the programmer partitions the input data, assigns each partition
1683	to a specific PIM address, and transfers the partitioned data
1684	to the corresponding PIM core. To maintain the integrity of
1685	the offloading process and to ensure that all input data are
1686	transferred correctly, the programmer must carefully assign
1687	each segment of the partitioned data to a unique PIM address.
1688	Consequently, each segment stored within the PIM address
1689	space is mapped independently to other segments.
1690	With such property in mind, recall from our discussion
1691	in Section III-B (Figure 5) where we root-caused the reason behind PIM’s sub-optimal read/write throughput to the
1692	following two factors: (1) the software-level multi-threaded
1693	DRAM↔PIM data transfer, and (2) the fact that the OS
1694	thread scheduling policy issues data transfer threads in
1695	coarse granularity, failing to evenly distribute read/write traffic
1696	across the memory channels (Figure 12(a)). Our PIM-MS
1697	is designed to overcome such limitation by employing a
1698	“hardware-level” fine-grained memory scheduling that maximizes MLP (Figure 12(b)). As explained in Section IV-B, upon
1699	a DRAM→PIM data transfer, the pim_mmu_transfer API
1700	is invoked using a single thread that relays all source and
1701	destination addresses to the DCE. Therefore, when the OS
1702	schedules this (single) thread for execution, the source and
1703	
1704	destination physical addresses stored inside the address buffer
1705	gets translated into DRAM read/write requests that are targeted
1706	for all destination PIM banks (unlike baseline’s softwarelevel/multi-threaded/coarse-grained thread scheduling where
1707	the memory requests available for scheduling only target a
1708	single destination PIM bank at any given time). This in
1709	effect allows our PIM-MS to have much higher visibility
1710	and flexibility regarding which memory read/write requests
1711	to schedule to which PIM bank.
1712	Given this opportunity, PIM-MS employs a memory
1713	scheduling algorithm that exploits its enhanced visibility to
1714	maximize channel/bank-group/bank-level parallelism, aggressively reordering the sequence in which PIM read/write memory requests are issued to each PIM bank. We use Algorithm 1
1715	to describe PIM-MS’s scheduling algorithm. The input to
1716	Algorithm 1 is the contents stored inside the address buffer,
1717	as detailed in Section IV-C (Figure 11). During initialization,
1718	the metadata representing the number of bytes to be transferred to each PIM core (i.e., pim_cores[id].offset,
1719	the “Offset” field in the address buffer entry in Figure 11)
1720	is set to 0 (line 16-26). PIM-MS then seeks to maximize
1721	channel-level parallelism by concurrently issuing memory
1722	requests to all PIM channels (line 28). To minimize columnto-column DRAM timing delay (tCCD), PIM-MS prioritizes
1723	bank group interleaving by issuing successive column com-

1742	E. Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit (HetMap)
1743	PIM manufacturers adjust the memory mapping function to
1744	prevent conflicts between DRAM and PIM, which inevitably
1745	leads to decreased DRAM read/write throughput (Figure 8,
1746	Section III-B). To achieve the dual goals of preserving high
1747	DRAM throughput while also separating the physical address
1748	space for DRAM and PIM, we introduce a unique memory
1749	mapping strategy called HetMap. Illustrated on the right side
1750	of Figure 9, HetMap employs two separate memory mapping
1751	functions, each optimized for a different design objective: the
1752	physical address space reserved for PIM utilizes a localitycentric mapping (Figure 7(a)) whereas the physical address
1753	space allocated for DRAM employs an MLP-centric mapping
1754	(Figure 7(b)). Depending on what the physical address the
1755	incoming memory request is targeted for, HetMap dynamically determines whether the memory request falls within
1756	the address space of DRAM or PIM. If the memory request
1757	is targeted for the DRAM space, it is mapped using the
1758	MLP-centric mapping, which incorporates MLP-enhancing
1759	optimizations, i.e., XOR hashing and placing channel bits
1760	near the LSB. If the memory request belongs to the PIM
1761	space, the locality-centric mapping is employed which adopts
1762	a simpler memory mapping strategy, i.e., the order in which the
1763	DRAM hierarchy is laid out is preserved in the locality-centric
1764	mapping (referred to as ChRaBgBkRoCo mapping in the remainder of this paper). For example, starting from the MSB of
1765	the physical address space, channel bits (Ch) are mapped first,
1766	followed by rank (Ra), bank-group (Bg), bank (Bk), row (Ro),
1767	and finally column (Co). As the sub-optimal PIM read/write
1768	throughput observed in conventional PIM devices is due to the
1769	software-level/coarse-grained/multi-threaded data transfers (a
1770	limitation which our PIM-MS effectively addresses), HetMap’s
1771	locality-centric mapping does not degrade PIM throughput, a
1772	property we quantitatively demonstrate in Section VI.
1773	In terms of implementation complexity, HetMap is codesigned with the BIOS firmware and hardware microarchitecture as follows. During system bootstrapping, the
1774	BIOS identifies the memory system configuration (number
1775	of channels/ranks/. . .) as well as the total memory capacity
1776	available in both DRAM DIMMs and PIM DIMMs. After the
1777	memory configuration is identified, the BIOS firmware informs
1778	the CPU’s memory controller the range in which the physical
1779	address space is partitioned across DRAM vs. PIM. Following
1780	this procedure, the separate address mappings are established
1781	for DRAM and PIM which HetMap utilizes to enforce the
1782	locality-centric and MLP-centric mapping for PIM and DRAM
1783	access requests, respectively.

1808	F. PIM-MMU vs. Conventional DMA Engines
1809	To alleviate the performance overhead of memory copy
1810	operations (e.g., memcpy, memmove), there exists several
1811	Direct Memory Access (DMA) engines that orchestrate data
1812	copy without CPU’s intervention, e.g., Intel I/OAT [83], [108],
1813	[109], [116], Intel DSA [53], [69], and AMD PTDMA [21].
1814	One might wonder whether the challenges of DRAM↔PIM
1815	data transfers can be effectively addressed by utilizing existing
1816	DMA engines. However, memory bus integrated PIM systems
1817	have fundamental architectural differences compared to conventional systems without PIM, limiting the efficacy of these
1818	DMA engines. As discussed in Section III, data partitioning
1819	as well as transferring partitioned data in/out of PIM is at
1820	the programmer’s discretion, unlike conventional DRAM-only
1821	memory systems where the allocation of data, its partitioning,
1822	and its transfers are transparently handled at the hardware-level
1823	to maximize MLP. Consequently, current PIM systems rely
1824	on coarse-grained, multi-threaded data transfers to maximize
1825	MLP at the software-level. Because DMA engines are not
1826	designed to utilize this unique property of PIM systems for
1827	performance optimizations, they are not able to fully reap out
1828	the abundant parallelism inherent in DRAM↔PIM data transfers. As discussed in Section IV-D, PIM-MMU’s DCE and
1829	PIM-MS can collaboratively utilize such opportunity with our
1830	hardware/software co-design, maximizing memory bandwidth
1831	utilization for both PIM read and write operations.
1832	Overall, while some of the functionalities provided with
1833	DCE (especially its ability to independently orchestrate data
1834	transfers without the CPU’s assistance) does resemble those
1835	of existing DMA engines, the features provided with our
1836	PIM-MMU is far beyond what current DMAs are capable
1837	of providing, e.g., the fine-grained scheduling of PIM-MS
1838	and HetMap’s dual-mapping function. In Section VI, we
1839	quantitatively demonstrate the limitations of existing DMA
1840	engines vs. our PIM-MMU architecture.

D. PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS)
We now discuss the design principles behind our PIMMS. The key observation that drives PIM-MS’s design is
that memory transactions targeting the PIM address space
(for both reads and writes) during DRAM↔PIM data transfer
are guaranteed to have mutually exclusive addresses. Such
mutual exclusiveness ensures that there are no true data
dependencies across different PIM memory transactions. To
better understand this unique property, it is important to
understand how PIM programmers go about partitioning input/output data. Before computation begins on the PIM cores,
the programmer partitions the input data, assigns each partition
to a specific PIM address, and transfers the partitioned data
to the corresponding PIM core. To maintain the integrity of
the offloading process and to ensure that all input data are
transferred correctly, the programmer must carefully assign
each segment of the partitioned data to a unique PIM address.
Consequently, each segment stored within the PIM address
space is mapped independently to other segments.
With such property in mind, recall from our discussion
in Section III-B (Figure 5) where we root-caused the reason behind PIM’s sub-optimal read/write throughput to the
following two factors: (1) the software-level multi-threaded
DRAM↔PIM data transfer, and (2) the fact that the OS
thread scheduling policy issues data transfer threads in
coarse granularity, failing to evenly distribute read/write traffic
across the memory channels (Figure 12(a)). Our PIM-MS
is designed to overcome such limitation by employing a
“hardware-level” fine-grained memory scheduling that maximizes MLP (Figure 12(b)). As explained in Section IV-B, upon
a DRAM→PIM data transfer, the pim_mmu_transfer API
is invoked using a single thread that relays all source and
destination addresses to the DCE. Therefore, when the OS
schedules this (single) thread for execution, the source and

destination physical addresses stored inside the address buffer
gets translated into DRAM read/write requests that are targeted
for all destination PIM banks (unlike baseline’s softwarelevel/multi-threaded/coarse-grained thread scheduling where
the memory requests available for scheduling only target a
single destination PIM bank at any given time). This in
effect allows our PIM-MS to have much higher visibility
and flexibility regarding which memory read/write requests
to schedule to which PIM bank.
Given this opportunity, PIM-MS employs a memory
scheduling algorithm that exploits its enhanced visibility to
maximize channel/bank-group/bank-level parallelism, aggressively reordering the sequence in which PIM read/write memory requests are issued to each PIM bank. We use Algorithm 1
to describe PIM-MS’s scheduling algorithm. The input to
Algorithm 1 is the contents stored inside the address buffer,
as detailed in Section IV-C (Figure 11). During initialization,
the metadata representing the number of bytes to be transferred to each PIM core (i.e., pim_cores[id].offset,
the “Offset” field in the address buffer entry in Figure 11)
is set to 0 (line 16-26). PIM-MS then seeks to maximize
channel-level parallelism by concurrently issuing memory
requests to all PIM channels (line 28). To minimize columnto-column DRAM timing delay (tCCD), PIM-MS prioritizes
bank group interleaving by issuing successive column com-

E. Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit (HetMap)
PIM manufacturers adjust the memory mapping function to
prevent conflicts between DRAM and PIM, which inevitably
leads to decreased DRAM read/write throughput (Figure 8,
Section III-B). To achieve the dual goals of preserving high
DRAM throughput while also separating the physical address
space for DRAM and PIM, we introduce a unique memory
mapping strategy called HetMap. Illustrated on the right side
of Figure 9, HetMap employs two separate memory mapping
functions, each optimized for a different design objective: the
physical address space reserved for PIM utilizes a localitycentric mapping (Figure 7(a)) whereas the physical address
space allocated for DRAM employs an MLP-centric mapping
(Figure 7(b)). Depending on what the physical address the
incoming memory request is targeted for, HetMap dynamically determines whether the memory request falls within
the address space of DRAM or PIM. If the memory request
is targeted for the DRAM space, it is mapped using the
MLP-centric mapping, which incorporates MLP-enhancing
optimizations, i.e., XOR hashing and placing channel bits
near the LSB. If the memory request belongs to the PIM
space, the locality-centric mapping is employed which adopts
a simpler memory mapping strategy, i.e., the order in which the
DRAM hierarchy is laid out is preserved in the locality-centric
mapping (referred to as ChRaBgBkRoCo mapping in the remainder of this paper). For example, starting from the MSB of
the physical address space, channel bits (Ch) are mapped first,
followed by rank (Ra), bank-group (Bg), bank (Bk), row (Ro),
and finally column (Co). As the sub-optimal PIM read/write
throughput observed in conventional PIM devices is due to the
software-level/coarse-grained/multi-threaded data transfers (a
limitation which our PIM-MS effectively addresses), HetMap’s
locality-centric mapping does not degrade PIM throughput, a
property we quantitatively demonstrate in Section VI.
In terms of implementation complexity, HetMap is codesigned with the BIOS firmware and hardware microarchitecture as follows. During system bootstrapping, the
BIOS identifies the memory system configuration (number
of channels/ranks/. . .) as well as the total memory capacity
available in both DRAM DIMMs and PIM DIMMs. After the
memory configuration is identified, the BIOS firmware informs
the CPU’s memory controller the range in which the physical
address space is partitioned across DRAM vs. PIM. Following
this procedure, the separate address mappings are established
for DRAM and PIM which HetMap utilizes to enforce the
locality-centric and MLP-centric mapping for PIM and DRAM
access requests, respectively.

F. PIM-MMU vs. Conventional DMA Engines
To alleviate the performance overhead of memory copy
operations (e.g., memcpy, memmove), there exists several
Direct Memory Access (DMA) engines that orchestrate data
copy without CPU’s intervention, e.g., Intel I/OAT [83], [108],
[109], [116], Intel DSA [53], [69], and AMD PTDMA [21].
One might wonder whether the challenges of DRAM↔PIM
data transfers can be effectively addressed by utilizing existing
DMA engines. However, memory bus integrated PIM systems
have fundamental architectural differences compared to conventional systems without PIM, limiting the efficacy of these
DMA engines. As discussed in Section III, data partitioning
as well as transferring partitioned data in/out of PIM is at
the programmer’s discretion, unlike conventional DRAM-only
memory systems where the allocation of data, its partitioning,
and its transfers are transparently handled at the hardware-level
to maximize MLP. Consequently, current PIM systems rely
on coarse-grained, multi-threaded data transfers to maximize
MLP at the software-level. Because DMA engines are not
designed to utilize this unique property of PIM systems for
performance optimizations, they are not able to fully reap out
the abundant parallelism inherent in DRAM↔PIM data transfers. As discussed in Section IV-D, PIM-MMU’s DCE and
PIM-MS can collaboratively utilize such opportunity with our
hardware/software co-design, maximizing memory bandwidth
utilization for both PIM read and write operations.
Overall, while some of the functionalities provided with
DCE (especially its ability to independently orchestrate data
transfers without the CPU’s assistance) does resemble those
of existing DMA engines, the features provided with our
PIM-MMU is far beyond what current DMAs are capable
of providing, e.g., the fine-grained scheduling of PIM-MS
and HetMap’s dual-mapping function. In Section VI, we
quantitatively demonstrate the limitations of existing DMA
engines vs. our PIM-MMU architecture.

Starting with the “Base+D” design (i.e., baseline system
utilizing DCE’s DMA capability but without the hardwarelevel/fine-grained memory scheduling enabled with PIM-MS),
this design point functions as a proxy for conventional DMA
engines like Intel’s I/OAT [83] or DSA [53]. Interestingly,
“Base+D” actually incurs a degradation in data transfer
throughput for 7 out of the 10 experiments we conduct in Figure 15(a). Careful analysis of such phenomenon reveals that,
compared to “Base+D” (i.e., the vanilla DCE that does not
employ HetMap and PIM-MS), the baseline system that does
not utilize DMA actually does a better job in utilizing memory
bandwidth thanks to its AVX-512 based wide vector read/write
requests which are aggressively issued concurrently using the

“Base+D+H” design point is able to significantly improve the
DRAM read/write throughput (as demonstrated through our
microbenchmark study in Figure 14), but the improvement in

of MLP it can exploit. Once PIM-MS is employed, however,
the “Base+D+H+P” design (i.e., PIM-MMU) fully unlocks
the PIM read/write throughput and significantly improves the
performance of DRAM↔PIM transfers.

proposals in place (“Base+D+H+P”), PIM-MMU can significantly reduce data transfer latency which directly translates

justifying its adoption in memory bus integrated PIM systems.

VII. R ELATED W ORK
Data movement support. To alleviate CPU’s burden during
data movement operations (e.g., memcpy), there exists a
variety of DMA engines. These include Intel’s I/OAT [83],
[108], [109], [116] and DSA [53], [69], along with AMD’s
PTDMA [21]. Kuper et al. [69], for instance, highlights the
efficiency of Intel’s DSA in offloading DRAM↔DRAM data
transfers. Additionally, NVIDIA’s H100 GPU [18] introduced
a memory copy engine called Tensor Memory Accelerator
which efficiently transfers data between off-chip DRAM and
on-chip scratchpad. In general, the concept of offloading a

C. Implementation Overhead
Implementation of PIM-MS and HetMap is primarily dominated by logic gates, so PIM-MMU’s most significant area
overhead comes from the DCE’s SRAM buffers whose size
is 16 KB and 64 KB for data buffer and address buffer,
respectively. The area overhead of these buffers are evaluated

 pour et al. [31] employed multiple DRAM address mapping
functions, dynamically choosing the optimal address mapping
function at runtime based on the target workload’s unique
memory access pattern for improved DRAM performance.
Zhang et al. [111] proposed user-program behavior-aware
memory mapping, which can efficiently exploit channel-level
parallelism. Meswani et al. [84] proposed hardware/software
co-designed memory management for die-stacked DRAM. Li
et al. [80] introduced a hybrid memory management approach
that quantitatively assesses the performance gains of migrating
a page between various memory types within a hybrid memory
system. While these prior work bears some similarity with
PIM-MMU’s HetMap architecture, the unique aspect of PIMMMU lies in demonstrating the importance of synergistically
combining DCE, PIM-MS, and HetMap to fully unlock performance, rendering our contribution unique.

is similar between PIM-MMU and these DMA engines. However, as we quantitatively demonstrated through our ablation
study in Section VI-A (Figure 15, existing DMA engines are
not optimized to exploit the unique characteristics of PIM let
alone its implication from a system’s perspective, failing to
fully reap out MLP to accelerate DRAM↔PIM data transfers.
There also exists several prior work proposing architectures for
bulk data transfer acceleration [11], [30], [45], [100]–[103].
RowClone [101] and SIMDRAM [45], for instance, proposes
an in-DRAM bulk data transfer acceleration scheme where
multiple DRAM rows are concurrently activated as means to
enable fast row to row data copies. These solutions, however,
can only copy data between rows that reside within the same
DRAM chip, rendering PIM-MMU’s contribution orthogonal
these prior work as we focus on accelerating DRAM↔PIM
data transfers. These results highlight the unique contribution
and novelty of PIM-MMU vs. conventional DMA engines or
bulk data transfer architectures.
Characterization of commercial PIM device. Several recent work conducted a detailed characterization of commercial
PIM systems. For instance, [42]–[44] provides a detailed
workload characterization on the UPMEM-PIM system with
another line of research investigating how to exploit the
UPMEM-PIM system to accelerate data-intensive workloads,
e.g., dense/sparse linear algebra, databases, data analytics,
graph processing, bioinformatics, image processing, compression, simulation, and encryption [6], [7], [14], [20], [25], [41],
[57], [59], [60], [74], [81], [87], [88]. There also exists a
series of studies exploring the hardware/software architectural
support for Samsung’s HBM-PIM architecture [71], [77], as
well as studies on using Samsung’s near-memory processing
based AxDIMM for accelerating recommendation models [64]
and database operations [75]. While these prior work provide
invaluable insights on commercial PIM devices, to the best
of our knowledge, PIM-MMU, which is an extension of our
prior work [76], is the first to uncover the unique systemlevel challenges of DRAM↔PIM data transfers in memory
bus integrated PIM systems.
Memory management for PIM systems. Prior work explored the designs of memory management targeting PIM
systems [5], [8], [9], [16], [23], [34], [46], [49], [50], [112].
Hall et al. [46] described memory management requirements
associated with virtual memory, specifically for the Data IntenSive Architecture (DIVA) [27]. Azarkhish et al. [5] presented
a zero-copy pointer passing mechanism to allow low overhead
data sharing between the host and PIM with virtual memory
support. Zhang et al. [112] presented an IOMMU design that
efficiently handles massive memory requests while supporting
virtual memory for PIM. While these works present memory
management schemes for PIM-enabled systems, they mainly
focus on aspects related to virtual memory, distinguishing
PIM-MMU’s contribution from them.
Memory mapping. There also exists several prior work
exploring efficient memory mapping architectures [4], [12],
[26], [31], [61], [62], [80], [82], [84], [111], [115]. Ghasem-

VIII. C ONCLUSION
Current PIM-integrated systems suffer from high performance overheads during DRAM↔PIM data transfers. We
propose PIM-MMU, a hardware/software co-design that enables energy-efficient data transfers in memory bus integrated
PIM. Compared to baseline, PIM-MMU incurs negligible
implementation overheads while providing energy-efficiency
improvements in DRAM↔PIM data transfers, leading to an
end-to-end 2.2× speedup for real-world PIM workloads.

Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the paper. Let me summarize the key information for the experiment and design idea outputs:

**Paper**: PIM-MMU: A Memory Management Unit for Accelerating Data Transfers in Commercial PIM Systems
- Conference: MICRO 2024
- Authors: Dongjae Lee, Bongjoon Hyun, Taehun Kim, Minsoo Rhu (KAIST)

**Key Contributions**:
1. In-depth characterization of UPMEM-PIM's DRAM↔PIM data transfer bottlenecks
2. PIM-MMU architecture with three key components:
   - Data Copy Engine (DCE): Offloads data transfers from CPU
   - PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS): Fine-grained hardware scheduling for PIM data transfers
   - Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit (HetMap): Dual memory mapping for DRAM (MLP-centric) and PIM (locality-centric)

**Evaluation Methodology**:
- Real UPMEM-PIM system: Intel Xeon Gold 5222 + 3 channels DDR4-3200 + 3 channels DDR4-2400 UPMEM-PIM
- Simulator: Extended Ramulator (cycle-level simulation)
- Benchmarks: PrIM benchmark suite (16 memory-intensive PIM workloads)
- Microbenchmarks: CPU-DPU (from PrIM), custom memcpy benchmark
- Energy/Area: McPAT and CACTI (32nm CMOS)

**Key Results**:
- 4.1× average improvement in DRAM↔PIM data transfer throughput
- 4.1× energy-efficiency improvement
- 2.2× end-to-end speedup on real-world PIM workloads
- 0.85 mm² area overhead (0.37% CPU die size increase)

Now let me classify this paper into the experiment layers:

1. **硬件架构**: Yes - PIM-MMU is a hardware/software co-design with DCE, PIM-MS, and HetMap. They modified Ramulator simulator to model these hardware components. This is primarily a hardware architecture contribution.

2. **kernel调度**: Yes - PIM-MS is essentially a memory scheduling algorithm at the hardware level that reorders DRAM↔PIM data transfers to maximize MLP.

3. **Serving调度**: No - this doesn't modify serving frameworks.

4. **编译框架**: No - this doesn't modify compilation frameworks.

5. **算法pipeline**: No - this doesn't propose new ML algorithms.

6. **芯片设计**: Potentially - the DCE is integrated near the memory controller, and HetMap involves BIOS/hardware co-design for memory mapping. But it's more at the memory controller/microarchitecture level rather than chip design per se.

- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
  CACTI建模baseline DDR4 DRAM chip（16 banks, 16 mats/chip, 1024 rows/mat, 512 columns/mat, 22nm）的面积。MIMDRAM的额外面积组件建模：(1) mat isolation transistors——每个mat global wordline上添加的隔离晶体管；(2) row decoder latches——每个mat的局部row decoder latch存储row地址；(3) mat selector和matlines——subarray级别的mat选择逻辑和连线；(4) inter-mat interconnect multiplexers和wiring——global row buffer每4-bit sense amplifier组的2:1 mux。DRAM bank面积开销=1.15%。Synopsys Design Compiler综合chip select和mat identifier逻辑的Verilog RTL，65nm下面积825.7μm²，缩放至22nm=116.3μm²。整体DRAM chip (16 banks + I/O)面积开销=1.11%。MIMDRAM control unit面积通过CACTI估计=0.253mm²，transposition unit=0.06mm²（同SIMDRAM），CPU die总开销=0.6%。对DRISA和Fulcrum使用相同baseline DRAM dimensions和其论文报道的面积开销（21%和82%）进行area-normalized comparison。

- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
  开源：https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/MIMDRAM（含Verilog HDL源码、CACTI配置、gem5 simulator）。使用例子（DRAM chip面积评估）：(1) 定义target DDR4 chip parameters（16 banks, 128 mats total, 22nm）作为CACTI input →(2) 分别配置baseline DRAM和MIMDRAM的CACTI模型（MIMDRAM额外添加mat isolation transistor per mat, row decoder latch per mat, mat selector+maltines per subarray, inter-mat interconnect per bank）→(3) CACTI输出bank面积（baseline vs MIMDRAM: +1.15%）和total chip面积（+1.11%）→(4) Synopsys DC综合chip select/mat identifier RTL（65nm）→缩放至22nm（116.3μm²）→加入I/O面积 →(5) MIMDRAM CPU die control unit area = bbop buffer (2KB, CACTI) + mat scoreboard (128-bit SRAM, CACTI) + 8×μProgram processing engines (0.03mm² each, 基于SIMDRAM) + transposition unit (0.06mm², SIMDRAM) = 0.313mm² →(6) 对比Intel Xeon E5-2697 v3 die面积→0.6%。作用：以极小面积代价（1.11% DRAM + 0.6% CPU）实现MIMD PUD计算能力，验证MIMDRAM的area efficiency远优于DRISA（21%）和Fulcrum（82%），且performance per area最优（1.18× DRISA, 1.92× Fulcrum）。

- baseline方法是什么？
  PIM-based sparse attention accelerator（Samsung FIMDRAM [16]）：使用CSR格式存储稀疏attention矩阵S，在HBM2 memory bank的I/O电路中嵌入可编程计算单元（near-memory computation），通过Ramulator-PIM [14]进行模拟评估。baseline全栈执行例子（以BERT模型GLUE数据集推理为例）：**算法层**：使用Sanger [22]的quantize-and-pruning方法实现动态稀疏attention——对attention score matrix S执行剪枝得到稀疏mask M，将M应用于Q×KT（SDDMM）和S×V（SpMM）操作。S矩阵以CSR格式存储（column index list + value list + row pointer list）。**系统框架层**：论文未明确说明serving框架使用情况。**编译框架层**：论文未明确说明编译框架使用情况。**Kernel调度层**：CSR-based SpMM——将CSR格式S矩阵与dense V矩阵进行矩阵乘法，需逐行处理：第1轮取CSR第1行非零元素→row-wise remapping对齐列坐标→执行in-memory MUL操作（每个PE仅能访问local memory内的数据）→第2轮取第2行→...→共需n行迭代完成。CSR-based SDDMM——逐行遍历mask M控制Q与K的向量乘法，每轮处理1行（该行的非零元素数约2个for ω=n/8 sparsity），5轮迭代中仅有2次有效计算（无效bubble占比高）。每轮迭代涉及cross-bank/cross-rank数据访问（PE需访问其他bank的K rows），经memory controller和system bus传输，C/A bus冲突严重。**硬件架构层**：HBM2-based PIM架构——10GB HBM2 memory，每bank含500MHz on-chip logic unit（PE），PE仅能高效访问local memory bank数据。当PE需要访问其他bank的数据时（cross-bank或cross-rank访问），必须通过共享的memory controller和C/A bus，带宽远低于local access。论文实验显示on-chip PE idle时间超过40%的PIM chip runtime（因为等待cross-bank数据），且随着sequence length增加PE idle ratio不降。核心痛点：(1) **CSR格式破坏列坐标**——CSR按行优先存储导致左矩阵S的列坐标被打乱，无法直接用于矩阵乘法的坐标对齐（左列=右行），每次迭代需row-wise remapping开销；(2) **Row locality mismatch**——稀疏attention的非零值呈对角分布而非行/列分布（Longformer场景ω=n/8时中心对角线区域数据密度是其他区域的7×），CSR的行存储方式无法利用此对角局部性；(3) **Cross-bank通信瓶颈**——PIM架构中PE仅能高效访问local bank数据，需cross-bank访问时通过memory controller和system bus，成为瓶颈并随sequence length加长而恶化。

- 论文方法是什么？如何对应解决Baseline的缺陷？
  ASADI提出DIA-based compression + DIA-based in-situ computing paradigm + full-flow ReRAM accelerator的软硬件协同设计。全栈执行例子（以BERT模型GLUE数据集推理为例）：**算法层**：提出两种DIA压缩方法——(a) Classic Bubble-free DIA：对Longformer等静态稀疏attention，将沿对角线分布的每列填满非零元素的bubble-free diagonal直接按列存储。每列存储一条对角线（中心对角线DI0居中），行坐标为同一对角线上的元素col坐标。(b) Bubble-containing DIA：对Sanger等动态稀疏attention，选择中心ω=n/8条对角线作为ω区域，将ω区域外的非零值（灰色单元格）移到最近的ω对角线（保持原有列坐标，行坐标改变），用(Rd, Ro)列表记录灰色单元格在DIA格式中与原矩阵中的行坐标映射。保证NZω略大于NNZo以容纳灰色单元格。Decompressed DIA格式将相同行坐标的值行存同一行，减少了bubble数。**系统框架层**：论文未明确说明serving框架使用情况。**编译框架层**：论文未明确说明编译框架使用情况。**Kernel调度层**：DIA-based in-situ computing包含四个kernel：(1) In-situ SpMM (S×V)——利用DIA格式保留左矩阵S列坐标的特性（vs CSR破坏列坐标），直接进行in-situ向量-向量乘法，无需CSR的row-wise remapping。V矩阵每维度存于独立ReRAM array（共d个array），S的DIA向量均匀分布于各array（每array ωd向量）。每轮各array执行vec-vec乘法后将DIA向量轮换到相邻array继续乘法，所有对角线处理完后解压中间结果（按(Rd,Ro)恢复灰色单元格位置，按DI恢复中心对角线），最后in-situ vec-vec加法累加得Z。DIA迭代数仅CSR的1/7.5（Longformer场景）。(2) In-situ SDDMM (Q×KT)——Q和K同维度存储于同一ReRAM array，逐对角线遍历mask M。每轮取一条对角线向量Mi连同(Rd,Ro)列表发送到row selector→按DI上下移位Q向量→按(Rd,Ro)执行memory copy→in-situ vec-vec乘法得SlicesSi→所有slice传输至对应array后in-situ加法得DIA格式S。每轮DIA迭代5次有效计算 vs CSR每轮2次有效计算。(3) In-situ Softmax——在ReRAM array内实现Max查找（逐bit从MSB到LSB过滤非最大值行，32 cycle for 32-bit float）和指数计算（逐bit左移实现2^x，32 cycle for ex）。(4) Analog Linear Layer——利用analog ReRAM crossbar的VMM并行计算Q/K/V矩阵，1 cycle处理1个embedding。**硬件架构层**：ASADI full-flow in-situ computing accelerator——12 En-PE + 12 De-PE，每En-PE含12 Tile（对应12 heads），每Tile含2个analog module（read-only ReRAM存WQ/WK/WV权重，执行linear/feed-forward层）+ 1个digital module（write-enable ReRAM 512×1024×1024 arrays存Q/K/V/S中间矩阵，执行multi-head attention）+ 1个microcontroller（管理压缩/解压和控制信号）。关键硬件特性：(a) Processing-using-memory (PUM)——所有计算在存储数据的ReRAM cell内原位完成，无需将中间矩阵搬出memory，消除cross-bank/cross-rank通信；(b) 每个ReRAM row独立并行操作——相当于每个row是一个PE，longer sequences增加存放数据的ReRAM rows数即增加PE数，并行度随sequence length增长（vs PIM的固定bank数PE）；(c) 内存复杂度O(n)而非O(n^2)，通过ω=n/8控制。对比baseline解决：**(1) DIA格式解决CSR列坐标破坏→** DIA按对角线存储保持列坐标顺序，无需row-wise remapping即可直接对齐矩阵乘法坐标，消除坐标对齐开销。**(2) DIA利用对角局部性解决row locality mismatch→** 对角分布使DIA格式每列含更多非零元素（Longformer场景DIA列均5元素 vs CSR行均2元素），每次in-situ操作有效计算2.5×更多，迭代次数降低（DIA只需2轮 vs CSR需5轮）。**(3) Full-flow in-situ computing解决cross-bank通信瓶颈→** 所有中间矩阵在存储位置原位计算，无需cross-bank/cross-rank传输，PE idle时间从>40%降至几乎为0。内存控制器不再是瓶颈。实验结果：平均18.6× speedup和2.9× energy saving vs PIM baseline；speedup随sequence length增长（GLUE上2.1× → Syn-8K上63.7×）；vs GPU RTX A6000、SPRINT、CPSAA均展现显著优势。

## PIM-MMU: A Memory Management Unit for Accelerating Data Transfers in Commercial PIM Systems

- 属于硬件架构的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
  PIM-MMU提出三个硬件组件的协同设计：(1) Data Copy Engine (DCE)——硬件数据拷贝引擎，完全卸载DRAM↔PIM数据传输，包含AGU（地址生成单元）、16KB data buffer、64KB address buffer、预处理单元（硬件级data transpose）；(2) PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS)——硬件级细粒度内存调度器，集成在DCE内部，利用PIM数据传输的mutually exclusive地址特性进行激进的request reordering以最大化channel/bank-group/bank-level并行度；(3) Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit (HetMap)——异构内存映射单元，维护双套内存映射函数：DRAM地址空间使用MLP-centric mapping（XOR hashing + channel bits靠LSB），PIM地址空间使用locality-centric mapping（ChRaBgBkRoCo顺序）。实验比较baseline UPMEM-PIM vs PIM-MMU的DRAM↔PIM数据传输吞吐量、能耗、端到端性能，以及消融实验（Base → Base+D → Base+D+H → Base+D+H+P）。

- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
  Ramulator [68] (https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator)，论文扩展Ramulator实现PIM-MMU的cycle-level模拟。McPAT [79] 用于能耗估算，CACTI [85] 用于面积估算（32nm CMOS）。

- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
  Ramulator模拟DDR4-2400 DRAM/PIM memory系统的cycle-level行为（4 channels, 2 ranks per channel, 512 PIM cores）。论文修改Ramulator的内容：(1) 建模baseline UPMEM-PIM的dpu_push_xfer数据传输——编译runtime library的dpu_push_xfer函数（gcc 9.4.0），提取CPU instruction trace，通过Ramulator的CPU-trace driven模式模拟；因Ramulator不支持AVX指令，将AVX vector load/store建模为"wide" 64B non-cacheable read/write（PIM access）和normal cacheable 8B read/write（DRAM access）；配置8核并发执行8个数据传输线程，OS线程调度建模为每1.5ms round-robin preemption。(2) 建模PIM-MMU——在Ramulator内实现DCE（AGU + data buffer + address buffer + preprocessing unit）的cycle-level行为、PIM-MS的Algorithm 1调度逻辑、HetMap的双套映射函数。(3) 能耗：用McPAT估算CPU core/LLC/memory controller的动态和静态能耗（基于simulated cycle count和activity factor），用CACTI估算DCE的16KB data buffer和64KB address buffer的SRAM面积和能耗。

- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。

```md
## PIM-MMU: A Memory Management Unit for Accelerating Data Transfers in Commercial PIM Systems

- 属于kernel调度/运行时计算的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
  PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS) 是PIM-MMU中的核心调度组件，将baseline的software-level/coarse-grained/multi-threaded PIM数据传输转变为hardware-level/fine-grained memory scheduling。PIM-MS基于以下关键观察设计：DRAM↔PIM数据传输中不同PIM core的memory transaction具有mutually exclusive地址（无true data dependency），因此可以激进地重排序memory request的发射顺序。PIM-MS的调度算法（Algorithm 1）：(1) 初始化阶段——通过get_pim_core_id(ra, bg, bk)函数为每个PIM core建立(rank, bank_group, bank)标识；(2) 调度阶段——do-parallel per channel并发地向所有PIM channels发射memory request（最大化channel-level parallelism），内层循环按bank group遍历（优先bank group interleaving以最小化tCCD column-to-column延迟），最内层在AGU翻译后的DRAM地址上最小化row buffer冲突同时最大化bank-level parallelism。实验比较：(1) baseline UPMEM-PIM的软件多线程粗粒度调度（OS CFS scheduler，每1.5ms round-robin preemption，8线程并发，线程与PIM channel/bank的映射由OS决定）vs PIM-MS硬件细粒度调度；(2) 消融实验Base → Base+D (only DMA without PIM-MS) → Base+D+H (DMA+HetMap, still software scheduling) → Base+D+H+P (full PIM-MMU with PIM-MS) 验证PIM-MS是吞吐量提升的关键enabler。

- 后端平台是什么，配置是什么。
  UPMEM-PIM商用系统：Intel Xeon Gold 5222 CPU (8 cores, 3.2GHz, 4-wide OoO, 224 entry instruction window, 64 MSHRs per core) + 3 channels DDR4-3200 DRAM (76.8 GB/s) + 3 channels DDR4-2400 UPMEM-PIM (57.6 GB/s, 512 PIM cores total, 每chip 8 PIM cores, 每PIM core对应1 DRAM bank, 每PIM core峰值1 GB/s)。模拟器配置：DDR4-2400, 4 channels, 2 ranks/channel, 512 PIM cores。

- 评估性能的软件/脚本是什么。修改了什么。

- 开源情况。评估软件/脚本如何使用？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
  PrIM benchmarks开源：https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/prim-benchmarks。使用例子：(1) 执行CPU-DPU microbenchmark：配置XFER_PER_BANK参数 → 调用dpu_push_xfer API（baseline多线程方式）或pim_mmu_transfer API（PIM-MMU方式）→ 测量DRAM→PIM和PIM→DRAM数据传输时间 → 计算throughput (GB/s) → 对比theoretical peak bandwidth得到utilization。(2) 执行PrIM workloads端到端测试：在真实UPMEM-PIM硬件上测量PIM kernel execution time（wall-clock time），数据传输时间根据simulation结果进行scaling（baseline vs PIM-MMU的比例）→ 组合得到end-to-end execution time → 归一化比较。作用：量化PIM-MS的硬件细粒度调度 vs baseline软件粗粒度调度在PIM read/write throughput上的提升（baseline PIM write仅15.5% bandwidth utilization → PIM-MMU显著提升）。
```

  PIM-MMU提出三个硬件组件的软硬件协同设计：(1) Data Copy Engine (DCE)——硬件数据拷贝引擎，完全卸载DRAM↔PIM数据传输，包含AGU（地址生成单元）、16KB data buffer、64KB address buffer、预处理单元（硬件级data transpose on-the-fly，解决UPMEM-PIM chip interleaving导致的data word跨chip分散问题）；(2) PIM-aware Memory Scheduler (PIM-MS)——硬件级细粒度内存调度器，集成在DCE内部，利用PIM数据传输中不同PIM core目标地址的mutually exclusive特性（无true data dependency），激进地重排序memory read/write request的发射顺序以最大化channel/bank-group/bank-level MLP；(3) Heterogeneous Memory Mapping Unit (HetMap)——异构内存映射单元，与BIOS firmware和memory controller co-design，维护双套内存映射函数：DRAM地址空间使用MLP-centric mapping（XOR hashing + channel bits靠LSB），PIM地址空间使用locality-centric mapping（ChRaBgBkRoCo顺序，地址按channel→rank→bank_group→bank→row→column从MSB到LSB排列）。DCE通过MMIO（memory-mapped I/O）注册为I/O设备，配备PIM-MMU device driver实现kernel-level MMIO通信。软件接口为pim_mmu_transfer API（单线程调用，传递pim_mmu_op struct包含传输方向、per-bank传输大小、源/目标地址数组）。实验比较：(1) baseline UPMEM-PIM vs PIM-MMU的DRAM↔PIM数据传输吞吐量（1MB-256MB不同传输大小）；(2) baseline vs PIM-MMU在CPU/内存资源竞争场景下的鲁棒性；(3) 消融实验Base → Base+D (only DCE DMA without PIM-MS) → Base+D+H (DMA+HetMap) → Base+D+H+P (full PIM-MMU) 逐步验证各组件的贡献；(4) 16个PrIM real-world PIM workload的端到端性能。

- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
  Ramulator [68] (https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator)，论文扩展Ramulator实现PIM-MMU的cycle-level行为模拟。McPAT [79] 用于能耗估算，CACTI [85] 用于面积估算（32nm CMOS下DCE的SRAM buffer面积=0.85mm²，仅0.37% CPU die面积增加）。

- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
  Ramulator模拟DDR4-2400 DRAM/PIM memory system的cycle-level行为（4 channels, 2 ranks/channel, 512 PIM cores, FR-FCFS memory scheduler）。论文对Ramulator的修改：(1) Baseline UPMEM-PIM模拟——编译UPMEM-PIM runtime library的dpu_push_xfer函数（gcc 9.4.0），提取CPU instruction trace通过Ramulator CPU-trace driven模式执行；因Ramulator不支持AVX指令，将AVX-512 vector load/store建模为"wide" 64B non-cacheable read/write（PIM access，bypass cache）和normal cacheable 8B read/write（DRAM access）；配置8核并发执行8个PIM数据传输线程，OS CFS线程调度建模为每1.5ms round-robin preemption。(2) PIM-MMU模拟——在Ramulator内实现DCE的cycle-level行为（AGU地址翻译 + 16KB data buffer读写 + 64KB address buffer管理含DRAM addr/PIM addr/Offset字段 + preprocessing unit的on-the-fly transpose）；PIM-MS的Algorithm 1调度逻辑（do-parallel per channel → per bank group interleaving → per bank，利用address buffer中所有PIM core的目标地址可见性进行request reordering）；HetMap的双套映射函数（DRAM侧MLP-centric with XOR hashing，PIM侧ChRaBgBkRoCo locality-centric）。(3) 能耗模拟——McPAT估算CPU core/LLC/memory controller的动态和静态能耗（基于simulated cycle count和activity factor），CACTI估算DCE的16KB data buffer + 64KB address buffer的SRAM能耗和面积。

- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
  PIM-MMU论文未明确说明是否开源。已知开源依赖：Ramulator (https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator)，PrIM benchmarks (https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/prim-benchmarks)。使用例子：(1) 配置Ramulator模拟baseline UPMEM-PIM：设置4 channels DDR4-2400, 2 ranks/channel, 8-core 3.2GHz OoO CPU with 64 MSHRs, FR-FCFS scheduler, locality-centric memory mapping（BIOS 1-way IMC + 1-way channel interleaving）→ 编译UPMEM-PIM runtime dpu_push_xfer提取instruction trace → Ramulator CPU-trace mode执行 → 获得baseline DRAM→PIM/PIM→DRAM数据传输的per-channel throughput breakdown和cycle count。(2) 配置Ramulator模拟PIM-MMU：同baseline配置基础上，在memory controller侧建模DCE（16KB data buffer + 64KB address buffer, 3.2GHz），实现PIM-MS Algorithm 1调度逻辑，配置HetMap双套映射（DRAM侧MLP-centric, PIM侧ChRaBgBkRoCo）→ 运行相同microbenchmark和16个PrIM workload → 获得PIM-MMU的数据传输cycle count → 用McPAT/CACTI估算能耗 → 对比baseline得到throughput提升（4.1× avg）、energy-efficiency提升（4.1× avg）、端到端加速（2.2× avg）。(3) 真实硬件测量：在Intel Xeon Gold 5222 + 3ch DDR4-3200 + 3ch UPMEM-PIM真实系统上用Intel PCM [55]测量系统功耗，用Intel VTune [56]测量per-channel write throughput。作用：在cycle-level精度上综合评估PIM-MMU三个硬件组件（DCE/PIM-MS/HetMap）对DRAM↔PIM数据通路中memory controller调度、地址映射、数据预处理和buffer行为的性能/能耗/面积影响。

27	- baseline方法是什么？

## TAIDL: Tensor Accelerator ISA Definition Language with Auto-generation of Scalable Test Oracles

- baseline方法是什么？
  学术张量加速器（如Eyeriss、MAERI、FEATHER）缺乏明确定义的ISA语义和快速测试预言（functional simulator/test oracle）。现有的手工测试预言如Gemmini Spike（基于RISC-V Spike扩展）和Intel SDE（基于Pin动态二进制翻译框架）是用C++手写的，单线程运行、由GCC/Clang等通用编译器编译，缺乏跨循环的优化，无法利用多核CPU或GPU并行加速。在模型推理全栈执行例子中：用户编写kernel → 编译器（如Exo）编译为加速器指令 → 利用手工测试预言逐个指令串行模拟执行以验证正确性 → 每次仿真需数秒至数分钟，大型kernel甚至超过1小时，无法集成到CI开发管线中。Programmability方面，缺少标准化的ISA语义描述格式，每个加速器需独立构建工具链，重复工程量大。Gemmini Spike在处理1024×1024矩阵乘法时需要超过1分钟，而简单的矩阵乘法只是ML工作负载中最基本的操作。

- 论文方法是什么？如何对应解决Baseline的缺陷？
  论文提出TAIDL——首个面向张量加速器的ISA定义语言，将ISA语义用高层次XLA-HLO张量算子（如dot_general、reshape、transpose、bitcast_convert等）描述，而非C风格标量代码。通过变换算法（transform，Figure 16）将kernel函数中的指令流自动转换为XLA-HLO计算图：控制寄存器/调用属性的assign和assert通过常量传播静态解析，tb_read/tb_write转为slice/dynamic_update_slice算子，hlo_op保持不变，REPEAT/IF块在编译时展开。生成的XLA-HLO图由XLA张量编译器编译为高度并行化的可执行文件，自动利用XLA的算子融合、代数简化、内存布局优化和自动并行化（多线程CPU或GPU kernel），实现比手工测试预言快3-4个数量级的仿真。
  全栈执行例子对比（Intel AMX tdpbusd指令）：**Baseline**: kernel中amx.api.tdpbusd → Intel SDE通过Pin逐条插桩每条指令 → Intel SDE串行C++仿真每条AMX指令的数据布局变换和矩阵乘法 → 输出结果。**论文方法**: kernel中amx.api.tdpbusd → TAIDL-TO变换算法将指令语义展开为XLA-HLO图（slice读取tile寄存器 → reshape/transpose进行数据布局变换 → convert进行类型提升 → dot_general执行矩阵乘法 → add累加 → dynamic_update_slice写回tile寄存器）→ XLA编译器自动融合算子、优化内存访问模式、生成多线程CPU或GPU kernel → 输出结果。对于1024×1024矩阵乘法，TAIDL-TO在GPU上仅需4ms（vs Gemmini Spike的>60秒），端到端I-BERT模型模拟仅需0.8秒（vs Gemmini Spike的>50分钟）。TAIDL是retargetable的——同一套变换算法适用于任何TAIDL定义的ISA，消除了为每个加速器重复开发测试预言的工作。

## BBS: Bi-directional Bit-level Sparsity for Deep Learning Acceleration

- baseline方法是什么？
  已有bit-serial DNN加速器（Stripes、Pragmatic、Bitlet、BitWave）仅利用zero-bit sparsity。Pragmatic按weight内的非零bit串行处理，但不同weight的非零bit数量不同导致负载不均，且需要variable shifter同步不同bit significance；Bitlet按bit-significance分组处理多个weight的同一bit位，但需要大multiplexer（64:1）选取对应activation，硬件开销大；BitWave采用bit-column粒度跳过全零列并结合sign-magnitude格式增强zero-bit sparsity，但需2's complementer支持sign-magnitude算术，且仍仅利用zero-bit方向稀疏性。全栈执行例子（以INT8 ResNet-50卷积层推理为例）：FP32权重 → per-channel PTQ量化为INT8（值稀疏度<5%）→ BitWave使用sign-magnitude格式翻转部分bit为0以生成更多zero bit columns → 权重存储于DRAM（压缩后bit columns + metadata）→ BitWave accelerator PE以bit-column-serial方式逐bit column读取权重 → sign-magnitude位串行乘法（需2's complementer转换部分和）→ 当某bit column全零时跳过整个cycle → 累加输出。痛点：(1) 仅利用zero-bit稀疏，负载随机不均衡；(2) 仍从off-chip memory读取所有bit；(3) sign-magnitude算术需额外2's complementer硬件开销；(4) zero-bit-only pruning在压缩时丢失量化级别，导致大绝对值区间KL divergence高。

182	## MIMDRAM: An End-to-End Processing-Using-DRAM System for High-Throughput, Energy-Efficient and Programmer-Transparent Multiple-Instruction Multiple-Data Computing
183	
184	- 属于硬件架构的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
185	  MIMDRAM是硬件/软件协同设计的PUD（Processing-Using-DRAM）系统，在DRAM subarray内引入细粒度DRAM激活，将传统PUD的very-wide SIMD执行模型改造为MIMD（Multiple-Instruction Multiple-Data）执行模型。硬件端实现包括：(1) DRAM subarray的三个新硬件结构——mat isolation transistor（分段global wordline以独立访问单个DRAM mat）、row decoder latch（存储局部row地址以供独立激活）、mat selector（断言一组mat isolation transistors，使能指定mat范围的PUD操作）；(2) 两种低成本interconnect——inter-mat interconnect（复用global row buffer sense amplifier的高驱动能力，加2:1 multiplexer实现跨mat数据传输，通过GB-MOV命令控制）和intra-mat interconnect（利用HFF latch/latch能力实现mat内跨列数据传输，通过LC-MOV命令控制，无需额外硬件修改），支持in-situ PUD vector reduction；(3) memory controller中的控制单元（bbop buffer、mat scheduler、mat scoreboard、μProgram processing engines），负责编排独立PUD operation在DRAM mats上的并发执行；(4) MIMDRAM transposition unit（从SIMDRAM的transposition unit修改，增加mat range信息以仅transpose mat范围内数据，无需填满整行）。实验比较：在12个真实应用上（Phoenix/Polybench/Rodinia/SPEC 2017）和495个多程序混合workload上，对比baseline SIMDRAM（state-of-the-art PUD framework）、Intel Skylake CPU、NVIDIA A100 GPU，以及DRISA和Fulcrum两种PIM架构。评估指标：SIMD utilization、performance、energy efficiency（performance per Watt）、throughput（weighted speedup）、fairness（maximum slowdown）、job turnaround time（harmonic speedup）、area-normalized performance per area。
186	
187	- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
188	  - gem5模拟器（周期精确全系统模拟器）：https://www.gem5.org/——用于建模MIMDRAM和SIMDRAM。配置为gem5 system emulation mode，x86 1-core out-of-order 4GHz，L1 Data+Inst cache 32KB，L2 cache 256KB，memory controller 8KB row size，FR-FCFS scheduling。内存配置：DDR4-2400，1 channel，8 chips，4 ranks，16 banks/rank，16 mats/chip，1024 rows/mat，512 columns/mat。
189	  - CACTI：https://github.com/HewlettPackard/cacti——用于DRAM chip面积和能耗建模，22nm工艺节点。
190	  - Synopsys Design Compiler（商业工具）——综合MIMDRAM的chip select logic和mat identifier logic的Verilog HDL设计，65nm工艺，缩放到22nm。
191	  - Intel RAPL——用于测量Intel Skylake CPU能耗。
192	  - nvml API——用于测量NVIDIA A100 GPU能耗。
193	  - 开源simulation infrastructure：https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/MIMDRAM。
194	
195	- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
196	  gem5模拟MIMDRAM和SIMDRAM在DDR4 DRAM上的端到端应用执行性能（execution time、cycles）。修改内容：(1) 在gem5 memory controller中加入MIMDRAM control unit（bbop buffer 2KB、mat scoreboard 128-bit、8个μProgram processing engines）；(2) 建模AAP/AP/GB-MOV/LC-MOV等PUD DRAM命令的延迟和能耗；(3) 建模fine-grained DRAM activation的开销（mat isolation transistor和row decoder latch增加的延迟<0.5% ACT latency）；(4) 建模SIMDRAM baseline（含back-to-back ACT latency为1.1× tRAS的验证）；(5) 模拟SIMDRAM和MIMDRAM的PUD操作执行（含vector reduction的GB-MOV/LC-MOV序列）。CACTI建模MIMDRAM的DRAM bank/chip面积开销（mat isolation transistors、row decoder latches、mat selector、matlines、inter-mat interconnect multiplexers和wiring）和能耗（每个额外simultaneous row activation增加22%能耗）。对DRISA 3T1C和Fulcrum的建模也使用了相同DRAM module dimensions（ranks/chips/banks/mats/rows/columns与baseline DDR4一致）。
197	
198	- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
199	  MIMDRAM完全开源：https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/MIMDRAM（含gem5 simulator修改、compiler passes、benchmark scripts）。使用例子：(1) 配置gem5 se mode + DDR4-2400 + MIMDRAM参数（8 entries mat queue, 2KB bbop buffer, 8 μProgram processing engines, 2KB mat translation table）→ (2) 用clang -O3 -Rpass=loop-vectorize编译目标应用（如Polybench 2mm）→ (3) MIMDRAM compiler passes自动vectorize循环并生成bbop指令→ (4) gem5+ MIMDRAM执行binary：host CPU dispatch bbop指令到MIMDRAM control unit → control unit的mat scheduler用online first fit算法分配μProgram到处理引擎→处理引擎将bbop翻译为AAP/AP序列→DRAM chip通过mat selector+mat isolation transistors仅激活目标mat range执行PUD操作→(5) gem5输出cycle-level execution time和能耗（CACTI模型）→(6) 对比SIMDRAM/CPU/GPU baselines。作用：提供完整的PUD MIMD系统仿真平台，验证MIMDRAM硬件修改（1.11% DRAM chip area, 0.6% CPU die area）的可行性和性能收益（34× performance, 14.3× energy efficiency over SIMDRAM）。
200	
201	## ASADI: Accelerating Sparse Attention using Diagonal-based In-situ Computing
202	
203	- 属于硬件架构的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
204	  提出ASADI full-flow in-situ computing accelerator架构，所有Transformer计算（线性层、Q×KT、softmax、S×V）均在ReRAM array内原位完成，无需将中间矩阵搬出memory，消除cross-bank/cross-rank数据传输。架构组成：(1) Chip级——12个En-PE + 12个De-PE（支持Transformer Encoder/Decoder数量扩展），单一I/O接口接收输入序列；(2) En-PE级——12个Tile（对应12个attention heads），每Tile含2个analog module + 1个digital module + 1个microcontroller；(3) Analog module——read-only ReRAM arrays存储weight matrices（WQ/WK/WV），执行linear layer和feed-forward layer的VMM操作，含IR/OR/ADC/DRV/S&A单元；(4) Digital module——write-enable ReRAM arrays存储运行时生成的Q/K/V/S矩阵，执行multi-head attention（SDDMM/SpMM/Softmax），含IR/OR/ADC/DRV/S&A；(5) Microcontroller——控制analog/digital模块间数据传输，管理sparse mask矩阵的压缩/解压（§III），发送四种control signals（S×V/Q×KT/linear layer/softmax）触发对应in-situ操作。数据流：(1) Cross-Encoder dataflow——batch间pipeline，Encoder i处理Batch j的同时Encoder i+1处理Batch j-1的输出；(2) Intra-Encoder dataflow——Phase 1 analog linear layer生成Q/K/V → Phase 2 digital multi-head attention → Phase 3 analog feed-forward层。实验比较：ASADI vs PIM baseline（Samsung FIMDRAM, 10GB HBM2）；ASADI vs sister systems（DIA-PIM和CSR-ASADI）；ASADI vs modern accelerators（NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU/SPRINT/CPSAA）。面积、功耗、memory breakdown见Table I。延迟/能耗breakdown（OCT/Linear/QK/Softmax/SV/CTRL）见Figure 22/23。Diagonal locality和sparsity sensitivity analysis。

207	  修改ZSim[30]（https://github.com/s5z/zsim，cycle-level microarchitectural simulator）模拟ReRAM array行为。自研in-house cycle-accurate simulator获取ASADI延迟和能耗（遵循Yavits et al.[42]数学证明）。Ramulator-PIM[14]（https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator）用于PIM baseline评估和diagonal locality analysis（图5中PE idle ratio）。ZSim修改内容未详细说明，论文仅提及"modify ZSim to simulate the behaviors of ReRAM arrays"。
208	
209	- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
210	  模拟ASADI accelerator的cycle-accurate延迟和能耗。延迟模拟：逐cycle跟踪IR/OR data caching、ReRAM array in-situ computation（vector-vector multiplication/addition/softmax）、ADC conversion、S&A移位加法、on-chip transfer (OCI)、cross-Encoder transfer (PCIe-6.0)。能耗模拟：累加ReRAM array read/write功率（SET/RESET 1.62/3.63V）、DRV activation功率、ADC工作功率、S&A单元功率、IR/OR SRAM buffer功率。PIM baseline通过Ramulator-PIM模拟：配置10GB HBM2 memory、500MHz on-chip logic per bank、CSR格式存储S矩阵、运行Sanger sparse attention workload。ZSim修改：论文未给出修改细节，仅表述为模拟ReRAM arrays行为。自研simulator的准确性通过Yavits数学证明验证。
211	
212	- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
213	  论文未明确说明ASADI自研simulator是否开源。已知开源依赖：ZSim（https://github.com/s5z/zsim），Ramulator-PIM（https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator）。使用例子：(1) ASADI simulator层面：配置12 En-PE + 12 De-PE + 每En-PE 12 Tiles → 按Table I配置各module的ReRAM array数量和尺寸 → 配置1T1M ReRAM参数（1-bit cell, 64×64 analog/1024×1024 digital, SET/RESET 1.62/3.63V, read/write column-parallel）→ 加载预训练的BERT/BART/GPT2/ViL weight矩阵到analog module → 加载DIA格式压缩的sparse mask到digital module → 按batch加载input embeddings → cycle-accurate执行Intra-Encoder dataflow (Phase1→2→3)→ 统计OCT/Linear/QK/Softmax/SV/CTRL各部分延迟和能耗 → 输出speedup和energy savings vs PIM baseline。(2) PIM baseline层面：在Ramulator-PIM中配置Samsung FIMDRAM → CSR格式存储S → 运行相同workload → 获得baseline参考值。作用：评估full-flow in-situ computing vs near-memory PIM在sparse attention计算中的性能和能耗收益。

  MIMDRAM完全开源：https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/MIMDRAM（含gem5 simulator修改、compiler passes、benchmark scripts）。使用例子：(1) 配置gem5 se mode + DDR4-2400 + MIMDRAM参数（8 entries mat queue, 2KB bbop buffer, 8 μProgram processing engines, 2KB mat translation table）→ (2) 用clang -O3 -Rpass=loop-vectorize编译目标应用（如Polybench 2mm）→ (3) MIMDRAM compiler passes自动vectorize循环并生成bbop指令→ (4) gem5+ MIMDRAM执行binary：host CPU dispatch bbop指令到MIMDRAM control unit → control unit的mat scheduler用online first fit算法分配μProgram到处理引擎→处理引擎将bbop翻译为AAP/AP序列→DRAM chip通过mat selector+mat isolation transistors仅激活目标mat range执行PUD操作→(5) gem5输出cycle-level execution time和能耗（CACTI模型）→(6) 对比SIMDRAM/CPU/GPU baselines。作用：提供完整的PUD MIMD系统仿真平台，验证MIMDRAM硬件修改（1.11% DRAM chip area, 0.6% CPU die area）的可行性和性能收益（34× performance, 14.3× energy efficiency over SIMDRAM）。

## ASADI: Accelerating Sparse Attention using Diagonal-based In-situ Computing

- 属于硬件架构的实现是什么？实验比较什么？
  提出ASADI full-flow in-situ computing accelerator架构，所有Transformer计算（线性层、Q×KT、softmax、S×V）均在ReRAM array内原位完成，无需将中间矩阵搬出memory，消除cross-bank/cross-rank数据传输。架构组成：(1) Chip级——12个En-PE + 12个De-PE（支持Transformer Encoder/Decoder数量扩展），单一I/O接口接收输入序列；(2) En-PE级——12个Tile（对应12个attention heads），每Tile含2个analog module + 1个digital module + 1个microcontroller；(3) Analog module——read-only ReRAM arrays存储weight matrices（WQ/WK/WV），执行linear layer和feed-forward layer的VMM操作，含IR/OR/ADC/DRV/S&A单元；(4) Digital module——write-enable ReRAM arrays存储运行时生成的Q/K/V/S矩阵，执行multi-head attention（SDDMM/SpMM/Softmax），含IR/OR/ADC/DRV/S&A；(5) Microcontroller——控制analog/digital模块间数据传输，管理sparse mask矩阵的压缩/解压（§III），发送四种control signals（S×V/Q×KT/linear layer/softmax）触发对应in-situ操作。数据流：(1) Cross-Encoder dataflow——batch间pipeline，Encoder i处理Batch j的同时Encoder i+1处理Batch j-1的输出；(2) Intra-Encoder dataflow——Phase 1 analog linear layer生成Q/K/V → Phase 2 digital multi-head attention → Phase 3 analog feed-forward层。实验比较：ASADI vs PIM baseline（Samsung FIMDRAM, 10GB HBM2）；ASADI vs sister systems（DIA-PIM和CSR-ASADI）；ASADI vs modern accelerators（NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU/SPRINT/CPSAA）。面积、功耗、memory breakdown见Table I。延迟/能耗breakdown（OCT/Linear/QK/Softmax/SV/CTRL）见Figure 22/23。Diagonal locality和sparsity sensitivity analysis。

- 模拟器名，模拟器链接（web search），或论文修改的模拟器。
  修改ZSim[30]（https://github.com/s5z/zsim，cycle-level microarchitectural simulator）模拟ReRAM array行为。自研in-house cycle-accurate simulator获取ASADI延迟和能耗（遵循Yavits et al.[42]数学证明）。Ramulator-PIM[14]（https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator）用于PIM baseline评估和diagonal locality analysis（图5中PE idle ratio）。ZSim修改内容未详细说明，论文仅提及"modify ZSim to simulate the behaviors of ReRAM arrays"。

- 模拟器模拟什么的性能，修改了什么。
  模拟ASADI accelerator的cycle-accurate延迟和能耗。延迟模拟：逐cycle跟踪IR/OR data caching、ReRAM array in-situ computation（vector-vector multiplication/addition/softmax）、ADC conversion、S&A移位加法、on-chip transfer (OCI)、cross-Encoder transfer (PCIe-6.0)。能耗模拟：累加ReRAM array read/write功率（SET/RESET 1.62/3.63V）、DRV activation功率、ADC工作功率、S&A单元功率、IR/OR SRAM buffer功率。PIM baseline通过Ramulator-PIM模拟：配置10GB HBM2 memory、500MHz on-chip logic per bank、CSR格式存储S矩阵、运行Sanger sparse attention workload。ZSim修改：论文未给出修改细节，仅表述为模拟ReRAM arrays行为。自研simulator的准确性通过Yavits数学证明验证。

- 开源情况。模拟器如何使用？作用是什么？基于开源文档和论文，使用例子解释。
  论文未明确说明ASADI自研simulator是否开源。已知开源依赖：ZSim（https://github.com/s5z/zsim），Ramulator-PIM（https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator）。使用例子：(1) ASADI simulator层面：配置12 En-PE + 12 De-PE + 每En-PE 12 Tiles → 按Table I配置各module的ReRAM array数量和尺寸 → 配置1T1M ReRAM参数（1-bit cell, 64×64 analog/1024×1024 digital, SET/RESET 1.62/3.63V, read/write column-parallel）→ 加载预训练的BERT/BART/GPT2/ViL weight矩阵到analog module → 加载DIA格式压缩的sparse mask到digital module → 按batch加载input embeddings → cycle-accurate执行Intra-Encoder dataflow (Phase1→2→3)→ 统计OCT/Linear/QK/Softmax/SV/CTRL各部分延迟和能耗 → 输出speedup和energy savings vs PIM baseline。(2) PIM baseline层面：在Ramulator-PIM中配置Samsung FIMDRAM → CSR格式存储S → 运行相同workload → 获得baseline参考值。作用：评估full-flow in-situ computing vs near-memory PIM在sparse attention计算中的性能和能耗收益。
